title: Fingerprinted bootstrap/main names plus full replacement of old files break reloads for up to 10 minutes after every deploy (stale cached index.html 404s)
description: The fingerprint step renames `main.dart.js` and `flutter_bootstrap.js` to SHA-suffixed names and rewrites index.html to reference them; the Pages upload contains only the new names, so the previous SHA's files disappear. GitHub Pages serves every file, index.html included, with `Cache-Control: max-age=600`, and the `<meta http-equiv="Cache-Control" content="no-store">` in index.html (line 21) is ignored by browsers for HTTP caching. A rider whose browser cached index.html in the 10 minutes before a deploy and who reloads (or whose installed PWA relaunches) gets the old index.html, which requests `flutter_bootstrap.<oldsha>.js` -> 404, so Flutter never boots; the HTML boot screen's 20 s fallback (index.html:144) then clears to an empty page. This directly undercuts the documented R-web promise that a live ride must survive a browser reload. Without fingerprinting a stale index.html would still have loaded the new main.dart.js.
failure_scenario: Rider opens the demo at 10:00, a push to main deploys at 10:03, rider's tab crashes/reloads at 10:05: index.html comes from cache, bootstrap 404s, 'Movera' boot bar runs 20 s then a blank page; their active ride snapshot is intact but nothing restores until the cache expires.
evidence: .github/workflows/publish-web-live.yml:92-105 `versioned_bootstrap = f'flutter_bootstrap.{version}.js' ... main.rename(build / versioned_main); bootstrap.rename(build / versioned_bootstrap); index_text.replace('flutter_bootstrap.js', versioned_bootstrap)`; lines 116-118 copy only the fresh build/web; web/index.html:21 `<meta http-equiv="Cache-Control" content="no-store">`; web/index.html:144 `setTimeout(clear, 20000);`.
suggested_fix: Keep the previous deploy's fingerprinted main/bootstrap files in the Pages artifact (e.g. carry over `main.*.dart.js`/`flutter_bootstrap.*.js` from the current web-live branch), or use query-string versioning (`flutter_bootstrap.js?v=sha`) like rider_map_camera.js so a stale index.html still resolves.

title: Fingerprinting step versions rider_map_camera.js but leaves movera_ride_snapshot_wipe.js cache-busted only by name
description: The step's own comment says 'Pages caches plain names: version the map gesture layer too', and it appends `?v=<sha>` to `rider_map_camera.js`. `web/index.html` line 147 also loads `movera_ride_snapshot_wipe.js` by plain name, and it is not versioned, so a changed wipe script can be served stale from the Pages/CDN cache after a deploy while the fingerprinted main bundle is fresh.
failure_scenario: A fix to movera_ride_snapshot_wipe.js is deployed; browsers that cached the previous copy (Pages serves plain-named assets with long cache headers) keep executing the old wipe logic alongside the new main.<sha>.dart.js until the cache expires.
evidence:
.github/workflows/publish-web-live.yml:108-112:
```python
          # Pages caches plain names: version the map gesture layer too.
          index_text = index_text.replace(
              'src="rider_map_camera.js"',
              f'src="rider_map_camera.js?v={version}"',
          )
```
web/index.html:147-149:
```html
  <script src="movera_ride_snapshot_wipe.js"></script>
  <script src="rider_map_camera.js"></script>
```
suggested_fix: Apply the same `?v={version}` replacement to `src="movera_ride_snapshot_wipe.js"` (and any other plain-named script in web/index.html) in the fingerprint step.

title: Documented live URL points at /-movera-rider/, the Pages build is published under /movera-rider-app/
description: ARCHITECTURE.md line 90 gives the live site as `https://baccarisverige-ux.github.io/-movera-rider/`. The publish workflow rewrites the base href to `/movera-rider-app/` (publish-web-live.yml:124) and the repository/Pages project is movera-rider-app, so the documented URL 404s. Per the ground rules, docs and code disagreeing is a defect.
failure_scenario: A reviewer or QA engineer opens the URL in ARCHITECTURE.md to verify the live build and gets a GitHub 404 instead of the deployed rider app.
evidence:
ARCHITECTURE.md:90:
```
https://baccarisverige-ux.github.io/-movera-rider/
```
.github/workflows/publish-web-live.yml:124:
```python
s = s.replace('<base href="/">', '<base href="/movera-rider-app/">')
```
suggested_fix: Change the ARCHITECTURE.md URL to `https://baccarisverige-ux.github.io/movera-rider-app/`.

title: QA_HOOKS.md says public release builds do not expose moveraOpenSafety, but bootstrap installs it unconditionally
description: docs/QA_HOOKS.md lists `moveraOpenSafety` among the hooks that public GitHub Pages release builds do NOT expose, and ARCHITECTURE.md states 'QA window.movera* hooks are gated (kDebugMode or --dart-define=MOVERA_QA=true)'. bootstrap.dart calls `installSafetyNavigationBridge(...)` outside the `moveraQaHooksEnabled` gate and `web_qa_hooks_web.dart` installs `window.moveraOpenSafety` with a comment that it is 'intentionally available in public web builds'; qa-live-rider-flow.yml even asserts it exists on public Pages. The code and the public workflow contradict the documented contract; one of them is wrong. The bridge can push the Safety hub over any screen from page script, so the doc readers' assumption that no navigation hook exists in release is false.
failure_scenario: An operator reading QA_HOOKS.md assumes `window.moveraOpenSafety` is absent on the public demo; on https://.../movera-rider-app/ `typeof window.moveraOpenSafety` is 'function' and calling it opens the Safety hub.
evidence: docs/QA_HOOKS.md:3-11 'Public GitHub Pages release builds do not expose: ... `moveraOpenSafety`'; lib/app/bootstrap.dart:76-78 `installSafetyNavigationBridge(() => pushPageOnce(() => const SafetyHub(), AppRoutes.safety));` placed before the `if (moveraQaHooksEnabled)` block at line 82; lib/core/debug/web_qa_hooks_web.dart:67-81 installs `'moveraOpenSafety'` with no gate; .github/workflows/qa-live-rider-flow.yml:118-119.
suggested_fix: Either gate `installSafetyNavigationBridge` behind `moveraQaHooksEnabled` (and drop the public-Pages step from qa-live-rider-flow.yml) or correct QA_HOOKS.md/ARCHITECTURE.md to list `moveraOpenSafety` as a release-available navigation bridge.

title: Cold start awaits push re-registration (Firebase init, getToken, POST /push/devices) before runApp, blocking the first frame on the network
description: `await _registerExistingPushSession()` runs before `runApp`. In staging/production with stored tokens and an accepted push consent it calls `PushPermissionGate.registerIfConsented` -> `FirebasePushService.register()` (lib/core/notifications/firebase_push_service.dart:198-227), which awaits `_gateway.initialize`, `requestPermission`, `getToken` (FCM network round-trip, no timeout in this code) and `_replaceToken` -> `_api.post('/api/v1/push/devices')` (ApiClient `_timeout` 15 s). Nothing in the app is painted until it resolves. The comment at lines 143-147 states the rider must not be kept waiting on push registration and defers `_pushCoordinator.start()` for that reason, but this earlier await defeats it. On the web the HTML boot screen's fallback timer (web/index.html:144 `setTimeout(clear, 20000)`) can remove the loading screen before Flutter paints, leaving a blank page.
failure_scenario: Production rider on a poor connection opens the app: the splash/boot screen stays up to ~15 s (API timeout) plus however long FCM getToken takes before Home appears; on web the boot screen can vanish at 20 s into a blank page.
evidence: lib/app/bootstrap.dart:130 `await _registerExistingPushSession();` ... :134-136 `runZonedGuarded(() { runApp(const MoveraApp());` ; :40-42 `await AppScope.instance.pushPermission.registerIfConsented(logEvent: 'push.session_restore_deferred')`; firebase_push_service.dart:210-226 `await _gateway.initialize(...); final permission = await _gateway.requestPermission(); ... final token = await _gateway.getToken(...); ... await _replaceToken(token.trim());`; api_client.dart:42 `static const _timeout = Duration(seconds: 15);`; bootstrap.dart:143-147 comment `...before anything slower runs, so the rider is not kept waiting on push registration.`
suggested_fix: Do not await it: `unawaited(_registerExistingPushSession())` after runApp (e.g. in the same post-frame callback as `_pushCoordinator.start()`), or run it with a short timeout.

title: A 401 on OTP verify while a token is still stored (auth preview / re-verification) is treated as session expiry: tokens are cleared and Sign in is re-rooted instead of showing 'wrong code'
description: `_send` enters the refresh/retry/expire path for any 401 whose request carried an access token (line 89); the comment relies on OTP verify never carrying one. `RideRestoreCoordinator` returns `SignIn()` when `AppEnv.current.authPreview && snapshot == null` (ride_restore_coordinator.dart lines 432-434, 449-452) without clearing tokens, and on web the tokens live in this tab's sessionStorage, so a reload with `?auth_preview=1` after an earlier sign-in reaches `PhoneVerify` with tokens present. A wrong code -> mock `401 invalid_otp` -> `_refreshAccess` (mock accepts any `mock-refresh-*`) -> retry -> 401 again -> `_expireSession` clears tokens, calls `onSessionExpired` (`LocationRepository.clearLastGoodFix()` + `showMoveraRoot(SignIn())`), then throws; `PhoneVerify` is unmounted so its `_error` is never shown.
failure_scenario: Web demo with `?auth_preview=1`: rider who signed in earlier in the tab types one wrong OTP digit; instead of 'wrong code' the screen jumps back to the first Sign in step, the stored session is gone and the last good location fix is wiped.
evidence:
api_client.dart:89-113 `if (response.statusCode == 401 && access?.isNotEmpty == true) { // An OTP rejection is not an expired session. Only requests that carried an access token enter the refresh/retry path. final refresh = await _refreshAccess(access!); ... if (replacement == null || response.statusCode == 401) { await _expireSession(replacement ?? access); } }`
ride_restore_coordinator.dart:449-452 `if (snapshot == null && AppEnv.current.authPreview) { reportRestoreSurface('signInPreview'); return const SignIn(); }`
suggested_fix: Exclude `/api/v1/auth/*` paths from the refresh/expire path (or let callers opt out), or clear tokens before showing the preview Sign in.

title: `POST /rides` answers `wallet_amount_invalid` as `invalid_request` with HTTP 409 instead of 400
description: `_validateQuoteBinding` returns `'wallet_amount_invalid'` for a wallet part that is negative, exceeds the fare, or is non-zero with `useWalletFirst == false` (lines 2247-2255). The route handler sets `status = 409` for every validation result and only swaps the code to `invalid_request` for this one (lines 598-606). CONTRACT.md §1: 'Validation ... are 400 invalid_request'; the mock's own `_error` doc says the code is the contract code. The response is therefore an `invalid_request` body with a conflict status, so a client branching on `statusCode == 409` (the quote-conflict re-quote path) treats a wallet validation error as a quote conflict.
failure_scenario: Demo flavor: a booking whose `walletAmountMinor` exceeds the quote total (e.g. after the quote was re-priced lower) gets HTTP 409 + `invalid_request`; the client's 409 handling re-quotes or reports a conflict rather than an invalid wallet amount.
evidence: in_process_mock_client.dart:598-606 `final validation = _validateQuoteBinding(body); if (validation != null) { status = 409; payload = _error( validation == 'wallet_amount_invalid' ? 'invalid_request' : 'conflict', requestId, reason: validation, message: 'Booking quote is missing, expired or does not match.', );`
suggested_fix: Use `status = validation == 'wallet_amount_invalid' ? 400 : 409` (and a wallet-specific message).

title: `PATCH /rides/{id}` offer raise / searching edit changes the fare, pickup and destination without `_touch`, so version, updatedAt, sequence and eventId stay unchanged
description: The non-routeChange PATCH branch (lines 947-1011) calls `_setFare(ride, fare + increase)` and rewrites `pickupAddress/pickupLat/pickupLng/destination*` but never calls `_touch(ride)`, unlike every other mutation (route change line 895, cancel via `_apply`, feedback line 646). The mock's own rule (lines 1351-1361) is 'one committed change: version + 1, new updatedAt, next sequence/eventId' and CONTRACT.md §1 requires a stale `expectedVersion` to be refused. After a raise the trip still reports the old `version`/`updatedAt`/`eventId`, so a second screen's `expectedVersion` from before the raise is accepted, `ApiRideRealtime` dedupes the projection by the unchanged eventId, and `updatedAt` misreports when the trip last changed. Reproduced: `AUDIT B2: fare 29100 -> 34100; version 1 -> 1; eventId ev_..._1 -> ev_..._1; updatedAt unchanged`.
failure_scenario: Demo flavor: rider raises the offer by 50 kr while searching; the projection's `version`, `updatedAt` and `eventId` do not move. A command sent from another tab/screen with the pre-raise `expectedVersion` is not refused as stale, and a polling consumer never sees a new event for the change.
evidence:
in_process_mock_client.dart:989-1010 `final increase = _offerIncreaseMinor(body, rideCurrency); final fare = _fareMinor(ride); if (increase != null && fare != null) { _setFare(ride, fare + increase); ride['offerIncrease'] = _money(increase, rideCurrency); } if (body['pickupAddress'] != null) { ride['pickupAddress'] = body['pickupAddress']; } ... payload = {'code': 'OK', 'ride': ride, 'requestId': requestId};` (no `_touch`)
in_process_mock_client.dart:1351-1361 `/// One committed change: version + 1, new updatedAt, and the next server-assigned realtime sequence ... static void _touch(`
suggested_fix: Call `_touch(ride)` after applying the offer raise / pickup / destination edit in that branch.

title: Route-change pricing double-charges stops that were already booked: `bookedKm` ignores stops while `routeKm` goes through them, and every existing stop is billed 25 kr again
description: `_ride()` stores `bookedKm` as the straight pickup->destination distance (lines 2319-2330) even when the booking body carries `stops` (which `_quote` priced through, via `_routedMeters`, lines 2103-2124 / 2134-2137). `_routeChangePricing` (lines 2046-2096) then prices a change as `bookedMinor + stops.length * 25 kr + (routeKm - bookedKm) * perKm`, where `routeKm` is pickup -> stops -> destination (lines 2071-2080). For a ride booked with a stop, a route change that keeps the same stop charges the stop's detour kilometres a second time plus a 25 kr stop fee that the quote never contained. The result is returned as `newTotal`/`difference` from `POST .../route-quote` and `PATCH .../rides/{id}` (routeChange) and, for non-cash methods, written as a `paymentAdjustments` capture (lines 919-932). Reproduced: booking pickup (59.3293,18.0686) -> stop (59.35,18.10) -> dest (59.3326,18.0649), fare 29 100 öre; route-quote of the identical route: `AUDIT B1: bookedKm=0.42 routeKm=5.69 newTotal=37900 difference=8800` (+88 kr for changing nothing).
failure_scenario: Demo/dev/test flavors (the stand-in backend the live GitHub Pages build uses). Rider books a multi-stop trip, then edits the destination by a few metres (or just re-confirms the same route) during the ride: the sheet shows a large surcharge (here +88 kr), and for card/wallet methods the mock records a captured adjustment for it. Money shown and 'charged' is wrong on every route change of a multi-stop trip.
evidence:
in_process_mock_client.dart:2319-2330 `'bookedKm': body['pickupLat'] is num && ... ? _km(body['pickupLat'] as num, body['pickupLng'] as num, body['destinationLat'] as num, body['destinationLng'] as num) : null,` (no stops)
in_process_mock_client.dart:2071-2087 `for (final stop in stops) { routeKm += _km(lat, lng, stop['lat'] as num, stop['lng'] as num); ... } routeKm += _km(lat, lng, dLat, dLng); ... final newMinor = rates.roundToStep((bookedMinor + stops.length * rates.convertKronor(25) + (routeKm - bookedKm) * rates.perKmMinor).clamp(bookedMinor * 0.5, double.infinity));`
suggested_fix: Store `bookedKm` from the routed distance through the booked stops (reuse `_routedMeters(body)`), and only add the 25 kr fee for stops that are new relative to the booked `ride['stops']` (or drop the per-stop fee, since `_quote` never charges one).

title: `restoreOnce` marks itself restored before the async load finishes, so concurrent first requests answer with un-restored defaults (fresh random PIN, empty contacts)
description: `restoreOnce()` sets `_restored = true` (line 49) and then awaits `PreferencesStore.load()` (line 52). There is no shared in-flight future. `InProcessMockClient.send` awaits `safety.restoreOnce()` per request (line 1208), so a second safety request that starts while the first one's load is pending returns immediately and `handle()` runs against the constructor defaults: `_newPin()` (a random 4-digit PIN), empty `contacts`, default `preferences`/`rideCheck`. Those defaults are what the client caches and shows; the restore then silently overwrites state afterwards (and a mutation made in that window is overwritten by `preferences.addAll(...)`, line 63). Reproduced with saved `movera_safety_demo_v1` (contact `ec_saved`, PIN 4321) and three concurrent GETs: `AUDIT C: first=[{id: ec_saved,...}] second=[] pin={... pin: 7214 ...}`.
failure_scenario: Demo build with `persistSafety: true` (the app's own transport). `WaitingForDriver.initState` calls `SafetyController.shared.load()` while the Safety hub (or ride-check policy fetch) also touches `/api/v1/safety/*` at the same moment on a fresh launch: the second chain gets no contacts and a PIN that differs from the one persisted/shown before the reload; a preference toggled in that window is lost when the restore lands.
evidence:
safety_mock_api.dart:47-52 `Future<void> restoreOnce() async { if (_restored) return; _restored = true; final generation = _generation; try { final prefs = await PreferencesStore.load();`
in_process_mock_client.dart:1208-1214 `if (persistSafety) await safety.restoreOnce(); final safetyHit = safety.handle(...)`
suggested_fix: Keep the restore as a memoised `Future<void>? _restoring` and have every caller `await` that same future (reset it in `reset()`), instead of a boolean set before the load completes.

title: Memory fallback on a failed secure save is never read back; a failed clear leaves the rider signed in
description: `save` catches a failure of the active store (Keystore/Keychain on phones, sessionStorage on web) and writes the tokens to `_memory` instead, but `readAccess`/`readRefresh` only fall back to `_memory` when the active store THROWS. A store whose write fails while its read answers normally (returns null) means the rider who just signed in reads back no session: `AuthRepository.hasSession()` is false and the restore gate shows Sign in again. Conversely `clear()` swallows a delete failure and clears only `_memory`, so after sign-out the real tokens remain and the next cold start (`_defaultHasSession`) goes straight to Home as the previous rider, defeating `UserDataWipe`. Reproduced with a throwaway test against `SecureTokenStore(override: ...)` using a store that throws on save/clear but reads normally: `flutter test` output `00:00 +2: All tests passed!` where the assertions were `expect(access, isNull)` after `save(access:'A1')` and `expect(await store.readAccess(), 'A1')` after `clear()` (log line `[movera:error] auth.token.secure_clear_failed {}`).
failure_scenario: Android device whose EncryptedSharedPreferences write fails (plugin throws) but reads return null: OTP verify succeeds, tokens 'saved', app immediately shows Sign in again on the next screen; or Keychain delete fails on iOS: rider signs out, data is wiped, relaunch opens Home signed in with the old tokens.
evidence: lib/core/auth/secure_token_store.dart:53-58 `try { await _active.save(...); } catch (...) { AppLog.error(...); await _memory.save(access: access, refresh: refresh); }`; lines 62-69 `try { return await _active.readAccess(); } catch (...) { return _memory.readAccess(); }`; lines 82-89 `try { await _active.clear(); } catch (...) { await _memory.clear(); }`.
suggested_fix: Track a `_memoryFallbackActive` flag set when a save falls back and read from memory while it is set; on clear failure rethrow (or retry) so sign-out does not report success while tokens persist.

title: LiveCancelFeePreview.freeMinutesLeft can go negative when the rule has no free window and the fee evaluates to zero
description: freeMinutesLeft is `fee.isPositive ? 0 : rule.freeMin - minutes`. The zero branch is meant for 'still inside the free window', but it is also reached when the computed fee is zero for other reasons (a rule whose fixed fee/percent resolves to 0 öre, or a zero fare), in which case `rule.freeMin - minutes` becomes negative once `minutes > freeMin`. Any UI that renders '{n} min free left' would display a negative number.
failure_scenario: Config publishes a live cancel rule with freeMin 2 and a 0-SEK fee for a promo category; 5 minutes after acceptance the preview reports freeMinutesLeft = -3.
suggested_fix: Clamp: `freeMinutesLeft: math.max(0, rule.freeMin - minutes)` independent of the fee sign.

title: ZoneClock.wallTime builds the zone wall-clock as a device-local DateTime, so a wall time that falls in the device zone's DST gap is silently shifted by an hour
description: `wallTime` computes the correct zone wall-clock components and then constructs `DateTime(year, month, day, hour, ...)` with the local-time constructor. Dart resolves a non-existent local time (the device's spring-forward gap) by shifting it, so when the device time zone differs from the zone's (RiderZones has Europe/Stockholm, Europe/Paris, Africa/Tunis; Tunis has no DST) the picker shows the wrong hour. `toUtc` (lines 74-86) uses `DateTime.utc`, so the round trip is asymmetric. Also the doc comment on `toUtc` says the summer offset is used in the non-existent hour, but the two-step guess yields the winter offset: wall 02:30 Stockholm on 2026-03-29 -> asUtc 02:30Z -> offsetAt = +2 -> guess 00:30Z -> offsetAt(00:30Z) = +1 -> 01:30Z (= 03:30 wall), not 00:30Z.
failure_scenario: Rider with a Swedish phone books a reservation in the Tunis zone for 2026-03-29 02:30 Tunis time (instant 01:30Z): `wallTime('Africa/Tunis', instant)` -> `DateTime(2026,3,29,2,30)` in Europe/Stockholm does not exist -> shows 03:30. The reverse mapping of the shown value then lands on a different instant than the one stored.
evidence: lib/core/config/zone_clock.dart:57-69 `static DateTime wallTime(String timeZone, DateTime instant) { ... return DateTime(local.year, local.month, local.day, local.hour, local.minute, local.second, local.millisecond); }` ; :71-73 doc `In the hour that does not exist (spring forward) the summer offset is used` vs :84-85 `final guess = asUtc.subtract(offsetAt(timeZone, asUtc)); return asUtc.subtract(offsetAt(timeZone, guess));`
suggested_fix: Return `DateTime.utc(local.year, ..., local.millisecond)` (a UTC-flagged carrier of wall components, which never shifts) and have the pickers treat it as offset-free; fix the toUtc doc comment or the algorithm to match.

title: ZoneClock.toUtc resolves a wall-clock time inside the spring-forward gap with the winter offset, contrary to its own contract
description: The doc comment (lines 70-72) says that in the hour that does not exist the summer offset is used. The implementation computes `guess = asUtc - offsetAt(asUtc)` and then returns `asUtc - offsetAt(guess)`. For 2026-03-29 02:30 Europe/Stockholm: asUtc=02:30Z -> offsetAt(02:30Z) = +2h (already CEST) -> guess = 00:30Z -> offsetAt(00:30Z) = +1h (still CET) -> result 01:30Z, i.e. winter offset. Verified by throwaway test: toUtc(DateTime(2026,3,29,2,30),'Europe/Stockholm') == 2026-03-29T01:30:00Z, expected 00:30Z. The UI pickers currently let the rider choose any wall-clock minute, so a non-existent time can be selected and the sent `scheduledPickupAt` is one hour later than the doc-specified mapping (and lands on 03:30 local).
failure_scenario: Rider books a book-later ride for 02:30 on 29 Mar 2026 (Stockholm). The wire time becomes 01:30Z = 03:30 CEST instead of 00:30Z = 02:30 CET-projected/summer mapping; the countdown and the server-side pickup differ by an hour from what the doc promises.
suggested_fix: After computing the candidate, check whether localOf(candidate) reproduces `wall`; if not (gap), use `asUtc.subtract(offsetAt(timeZone, asUtc))` (the summer offset). Also have the date-time picker reject or snap times inside the gap.

title: Driver-name fallback 'Driver' is English and is interpolated into translated sentences
description: MatchedDriver.displayFirstName and ReservationDriver.displayFirstName (reservation.dart:85-86) return the literal 'Driver' when the backend sends an empty firstName, while the ARB already has `driver` ('Chauffeur', 'Förare'). The fallback is injected into localized templates: waiting_for_driver.dart:1438 `context.l10n.etaLeaveNowName(driver.displayFirstName)` → 'Partez maintenant pour rejoindre Driver'; waiting_sheet_bits.dart:321 shows it as the name; upcoming_reservation.dart:504 `resYourDriverName(driver.displayFirstName)`; reservation_format.dart:282/288 driverChangedBody/driverLeftBody. Reproduced: L10n.use('fr'); MatchedDriver(id:'d', firstName:'').displayFirstName == 'Driver' while L10n.current.driver == 'Chauffeur'.
failure_scenario: Dispatch assigns a driver whose profile has no first name (firstName ''): the French Waiting sheet reads 'Driver' as the name and 'Partez maintenant pour rejoindre Driver'.
evidence: matched_driver.dart:37-38 `String get displayFirstName =>\n      hasFirstName ? normalizedFirstName : 'Driver';`; reservation.dart:85-86 same; waiting_for_driver.dart:1438 `: context.l10n.etaLeaveNowName(driver.displayFirstName));`
suggested_fix: Return L10n.current.driver as the fallback (both classes).

title: `MatchedDriver.fromJson` reads `id`/`vehicleMake`/... but the contract `DriverSummary` carries `driverId` and a nested `vehicle`, so a contract-conformant projection parses to no driver
description: The production transport `ApiRideRealtime` builds the driver from the projection with `MatchedDriver.fromJson` (api_ride_realtime.dart lines 201-204), as do `ride_projection.dart:68` and the restore path. `fromJson` requires `json['id']` (line 80, returns null when empty, line 83) and reads flat `vehicleMake/vehicleModel/vehicleColor/plate/photoAsset`. `contracts/openapi.yaml` `DriverSummary` (lines 5281-5305, required `driverId, firstName, vehicle`) and CONTRACT.md §2 (`DriverSummary { driverId, firstName, ..., photoUrl?, vehicle: { make?, model?, color?, plate? } }`) never send `id` or flat vehicle fields. The in-process mock sends `MatchedDriver.toJson()` (`id`, `vehicleMake`, ...), so the mock and the parser agree with each other but not with the shipped contract, and no test can catch it. Against a server that follows `openapi.yaml`, every projection yields `driver == null`.
failure_scenario: Staging/production flavor against a backend built from `contracts/openapi.yaml`: the trip reaches `accepted`; `ApiRideRealtime` emits `driverAssigned` with `driver: null`; Waiting shows 'Driver details unavailable' (no name, plate, vehicle, photo) for the whole ride, and the history/receipt has no driver either.
evidence:
matched_driver.dart:78-83 `static MatchedDriver? fromJson(Map<String, dynamic>? json) { if (json == null) return null; final id = json['id'] as String? ?? ''; final firstName = (json['firstName'] as String? ?? json['name'] as String? ?? '').trim(); if (id.isEmpty || firstName.isEmpty) return null;`
matched_driver.dart:90-94 `vehicleMake: json['vehicleMake'] as String?, vehicleModel: json['vehicleModel'] as String?, vehicleColor: json['vehicleColor'] as String?, plate: json['plate'] as String?, photoAsset: json['photoAsset'] as String?,`
openapi.yaml:5281-5305 `DriverSummary: required: - driverId - firstName - vehicle ... driverId: $ref Id ... photoUrl ... vehicle: $ref VehicleSummary`
suggested_fix: Accept `driverId` (and `photoUrl`, nested `vehicle.{make,model,color,plate}`) in `fromJson` alongside the legacy flat keys, and have the mock emit the contract shape so the contract tests exercise it.

title: window.moveraOpenSafety is installed in public release builds although docs/QA_HOOKS.md lists it among the hooks release builds do not expose
description: docs/QA_HOOKS.md:3-11 states public release builds do not expose `moveraOpenSafety` and that hooks install only under kDebugMode or MOVERA_QA. `installSafetyNavigationBridge` sets exactly that global without any gate, and bootstrap calls it unconditionally (lib/app/bootstrap.dart:76-78) outside the `if (moveraQaHooksEnabled)` block (lines 82-85). The gated `installSafetyQaOpener` (line 52) writes the same property name, so in QA builds whichever runs last wins. The code comment says this is intentional, so either the record or the code is wrong; per the audit rules a place where code does not do what the decision document says is reportable.
failure_scenario: On the public GitHub Pages build any page script (or the Maps JS SDK) can call `window.moveraOpenSafety()` and navigate the rider to the Safety hub; QA_HOOKS.md promises this surface is absent.
evidence: lib/core/debug/web_qa_hooks_web.dart:67-81 `void installSafetyNavigationBridge(bool Function() open) { // This bridge is intentionally available in public web builds. ... globalContext.setProperty('moveraOpenSafety'.toJS, ...` ; lib/app/bootstrap.dart:76-78 `installSafetyNavigationBridge(() => pushPageOnce(() => const SafetyHub(), AppRoutes.safety));` (before the `if (moveraQaHooksEnabled)` at :82); docs/QA_HOOKS.md:3-9 `Public GitHub Pages **release** builds do **not** expose: ... - moveraOpenSafety`.
suggested_fix: Either gate the bridge with moveraQaHooksEnabled (and use the gated installSafetyQaOpener only), or correct docs/QA_HOOKS.md / ARCHITECTURE.md to state that moveraOpenSafety is a public navigation-only hook.

title: reportSearchSnapshot is not gated, so release web builds publish the rider's pickup address and coordinates on window.moveraSearchSnapshotJson
description: Unlike `reportRideCheckSnapshot` (line 202, gated by moveraQaHooksEnabled) and the matching hooks, `reportSearchSnapshot` writes unconditionally. FindingDriverController._reportQa (lib/features/finding_driver/application/finding_driver_controller.dart:1670-1671) calls it on every tick with `qaSnapshot()` which includes `'pickupAddress'`, `'pickupLat'`, `'pickupLng'` (lines 1665-1667) and the rideId. ARCHITECTURE.md:20 says QA window.movera* hooks are gated. Any third-party script on the page (the Google Maps JS SDK is loaded on the same page) or a browser extension can read it in production.
failure_scenario: Production web rider searches for a driver: `window.moveraSearchSnapshotJson` on the public page contains their pickup street address and precise coordinates for the duration of the search.
evidence: lib/core/debug/web_qa_hooks_web.dart:83-85 `void reportSearchSnapshot(String json) { globalContext.setProperty('moveraSearchSnapshotJson'.toJS, json.toJS); }` (no `if (!moveraQaHooksEnabled) return;`, compare :202-205); finding_driver_controller.dart:1665-1667 `'pickupAddress': _snapshot?.pickupAddress, 'pickupLat': _snapshot?.pickupLat, 'pickupLng': _snapshot?.pickupLng,`
suggested_fix: Add `if (!moveraQaHooksEnabled) return;` to reportSearchSnapshot (and reportSafetySnapshot for consistency), as reportRideCheckSnapshot already does.

title: Public demo sends visitors' precise GPS coordinates to nominatim.openstreetmap.org with no notice
description: `AppGeocoding` is composed with `allowPublicReverseFallback: environment.allowsMockTransport` (di.dart:187-190), and the live GitHub Pages build is the demo flavor, so for every real visitor whose in-process reverse geocode answers the placeholder label the app issues a browser GET to `https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/reverse?lat=<6dp>&lon=<6dp>` — their exact position — to a third party, from the page the index.html shell itself documents as 'Do not expose rider addresses or coordinates to public browser-side geocoding services'. The code comment acknowledges the data flow but the public deployment is not a closed test environment, and no privacy notice covers it.
failure_scenario: A stranger opens the public demo link and grants location: their 6-decimal coordinates are sent to OpenStreetMap's public service on Home load (`detectCurrent` -> `geocoding.reverse`) and again on each pickup-label refresh.
evidence: lib/core/location/web_reverse_geocode.dart:14-20 `Uri.https('nominatim.openstreetmap.org', '/reverse', {'lat': point.latitude.toStringAsFixed(6), 'lon': ...})`; lib/core/location/app_geocoding.dart:125-129 `if (allowPublicReverseFallback && _isWeb && (named == null || named == placeholderReverseLabel)) { final street = await _publicReverse(point, ...)`; lib/app/di.dart:187-190; web/index.html:220-222 comment; .github/workflows/publish-web-live.yml:45-47 builds `-t lib/main_demo.dart --dart-define=MOVERA_FLAVOR=demo` for the public site.
suggested_fix: Round coordinates (e.g. 3 decimals) before the public lookup, or disable the fallback on the public Pages build and keep it for local dev only.

title: MotionEngine interpolation window starts at the previous GPS sample's timestamp, so lerp is always at t=1 and never interpolates
description: ingest() is called once per delivered fix (HomeController._deliverFix, lib/features/home/application/home_controller.dart:518) and passes `startedAt: _from!.timestamp` with a 420 ms window. `_from` is the previous accepted sample, whose timestamp is at least one fix interval (typically >= 1 s) old, so `now - startedAt` always exceeds 420 ms and the interpolator clamps to t=1, returning `_to` verbatim. There is no ticker that calls lerp between fixes, so the 'interpolation' is a no-op and the rider marker snaps to each raw smoothed point; heading likewise jumps. Not a crash, but the animation math does not do what the component is for.
failure_scenario: On the home map the blue rider dot and heading cone jump between 1 Hz fixes rather than easing across the 420 ms window.
suggested_fix: Record `startedAt = clock` when a new sample arrives and expose a `poseAt(now)` used by a frame ticker; or drop the interpolator if snapping is intended.

title: Firebase SW registered at the app's root scope makes Flutter's self-destructing service worker reload the page on every cold start of a Firebase-configured web build
description: `getToken` passes `serviceWorkerScriptPath: 'firebase-messaging-sw.js'` and firebase_messaging_web registers it with `navigator.serviceWorker.register(path)` and no `scope`, so the registration's scope is the app root (`/movera-rider-app/`). The build never passes `--pwa-strategy=none` (publish-web-live.yml line 45), so Flutter 3.47's `flutter build web` still emits `flutter_service_worker.js` and a `flutter_bootstrap.js` with `serviceWorkerSettings` (flutter_tools web.dart: `includeServiceWorkerSettings = strategy == offlineFirst`, compile.dart defaults to offlineFirst). Flutter's loader (`service_worker_loader.js` lines 105-113) calls `navigator.serviceWorker.getRegistration()` and, whenever ANY registration covers the page, registers `flutter_service_worker.js?v=...` at the same default scope, which replaces the Firebase registration's script. The 3.47 `flutter_service_worker.js` template is a cleanup worker: on activate it `unregister()`s and `client.navigate(client.url)` for every window client. index.html's cleanup (lines 169-176) deliberately keeps the Firebase registration, so on each boot where push consent was accepted: boot waits up to 4 s for SW activation, the page is force-reloaded mid-boot, the push subscription dies with the registration, and `_registerExistingPushSession` then re-registers the Firebase SW and POSTs a brand-new FCM token (`_replaceToken` only unregisters the previous token held in memory, so stale tokens accumulate server-side). The same `getRegistration()` path also fires once for demo visitors who still carry an old `flutter_service_worker.js` registration, because index.html's async `unregister()` races the deferred bootstrap.
failure_scenario: Staging/production web build with Firebase defines; rider accepted ride-update notifications. Every cold start: boot screen, 1-4 s pause, page reloads itself once, then boots; `/api/v1/push/devices` receives a new token on every launch and old tokens are never unregistered. If the reload lands during an active search, the search restores from the snapshot but the rider sees the app restart.
evidence: lib/core/notifications/firebase_push_service.dart:112-121 `_messaging.getToken(vapidKey: vapidKey, serviceWorkerScriptPath: kIsWeb ? moveraFirebaseMessagingServiceWorker : null)`; firebase_messaging_web-4.2.5 interop/messaging.dart:50-53 `navigator.serviceWorker.register(serviceWorkerScriptPath.toJS)` (no scope); web/index.html:172-176 keeps registrations whose scriptURL contains 'firebase-messaging-sw.js'; web/index.html:570 `<script src="flutter_bootstrap.js" defer>`; /opt/flutter/packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/web/file_generators/js/flutter_service_worker.js:7-30 `await self.registration.unregister(); ... client.navigate(client.url)`; engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/flutter_js/src/service_worker_loader.js:106-113 `getRegistration().then(registration => { if (registration) return registerAndActivate(); })`.
suggested_fix: Build with `--pwa-strategy=none` (or ship a custom web/flutter_bootstrap.js that calls `_flutter.loader.load()` without `serviceWorkerSettings`), and/or register firebase-messaging-sw.js under its own scope (e.g. `firebase-cloud-messaging-push-scope`) so the loader's root-scope `getRegistration()` finds nothing.

title: Telemetry sink and ApiClient build URLs by string concatenation; a base URL with a trailing slash passes the release validator but produces '//api/v1/...' on every request
description: `HttpObservabilitySink._post` does `Uri.parse('$baseUrl$path')` and ApiClient does the same (lib/core/api/api_client.dart:77 `Uri.parse('${_env.apiBaseUrl}$path')`, :189). `TransportComposition.releaseApiBaseUrlProblem` (lib/app/config/transport_composition.dart:18-31) is the fail-fast guard for an unusable MOVERA_API_BASE_URL and rejects empty, non-https and .invalid hosts, but accepts `https://api.movera.se/`. With such a define every API and telemetry call targets `https://api.movera.se//api/v1/...`; most servers/routers treat the empty first segment as a different path (404), and the sink swallows every error (`catchError((_) => http.Response('', 599))`), so a production build would fail every request at runtime, exactly the class of misconfiguration the validator exists to catch at composition time.
failure_scenario: Staging built with `--dart-define=MOVERA_API_BASE_URL=https://api.staging.movera.se/` passes AppScope composition, then every sign-in, quote and telemetry call 404s.
evidence: lib/core/observability/http_observability.dart:23 `Uri.parse('$baseUrl$path'),` ; lib/core/api/api_client.dart:77 `final uri = Uri.parse('${_env.apiBaseUrl}$path');` ; transport_composition.dart:18-31 (no check for a path/trailing slash).
suggested_fix: Normalise once (strip trailing '/' in AppEnv or reject it in releaseApiBaseUrlProblem) or join with `Uri.parse(baseUrl).resolve(path.substring(1))`.

title: After the not-found pause, a successful resync never restarts periodic polling: the ride freezes while the connection reports connected
description: `_endNotFound` (lines 347-353) cancels `poll.timer` and sets `poll.timer = null` after `notFoundLimit` consecutive 404s. `reconnectAndResync` (lines 379-390) only flips `poll.ended = false`, lowers `poll.notFound` and runs one forced `_poll`. Nothing re-creates the `Timer.periodic` that `subscribe()`'s `onListen` made (lines 69-77), and `onListen` does not run again because the broadcast controller already has its listener. When the forced poll succeeds, the success path calls `connection.markConnected()` (line 256) so the UI banner clears, but no further GET is ever issued for that ride: the Waiting/in-trip screen keeps showing the projection from that single read until the user triggers another manual resync. Reproduced with a throwaway test (3x404, resync -> 200, pollInterval 20 ms): `AUDIT A: events after resync = 1, state = RealtimeState.connected` then `AUDIT A: calls after 200ms of connected state = 4` (no new polls). Callers: `FindingDriverController` lines 897/1156/1288/1642, `WaitingForDriver` line 929, `RideRestoreCoordinator` line 167, `notification_navigation.dart` line 89 all use `reconnectAndResync` as the recovery path.
failure_scenario: Production transport (staging/production flavors). The trip endpoint answers 404 three polls in a row (replica lag, a brief routing fault). Polling pauses and the banner shows failed. The rider taps retry / the app resumes -> `reconnectAndResync` -> 200, banner says connected. From then on the driver's position, arrival, boarding and completion never arrive on this screen; the ride appears stuck at that status indefinitely although the connection state claims it is live.
evidence:
api_ride_realtime.dart:347-353 `void _endNotFound(_RidePoll poll) { poll.ended = true; poll.timer?.cancel(); poll.timer = null; ... connection.markFailed(); }`
api_ride_realtime.dart:379-390 `Future<void> reconnectAndResync(String rideId) async { ... if (poll.ended) { poll.ended = false; poll.notFound = poll.notFound > 0 ? notFoundLimit - 1 : 0; } await _poll(poll, force: true); }`
api_ride_realtime.dart:69-77 the only place a timer is created: `onListen: () { if (poll.timer != null) return; ... poll.timer = Timer.periodic(pollInterval, (_) => unawaited(_poll(poll))); }`
suggested_fix: In `reconnectAndResync` (or in `_poll`'s success path when `poll.timer == null` and the controller has listeners) re-create `poll.timer = Timer.periodic(pollInterval, (_) => unawaited(_poll(poll)))` once the forced read succeeds; keep it cancelled while `poll.ended` is true.

title: Mock driver is spawned and (on resume) walked to a hard-coded Stockholm pickup, not the trip's pickup; resumed matched rides also restart the accept/waiting clocks
description: `_pickupLat/_pickupLng` default to (59.3293, 18.0686) in both the resume path (lines 183-184) and `_assignNow` (lines 263-264), and the driver start position is derived from that default (`lastLat ??= _pickupLat! + 0.0072`, lines 209-210 and 265-266). The real pickup is only fetched by `_hydratePickup()` after the `driverAssigned` event (line 305) and never on the `primeResume` path; after a web reload the stand-in server is empty anyway so `_pickup()` 404s and keeps the default (line 660). `_startGps` therefore lerps toward and declares `driverWaiting` within 50 m of central Stockholm for a Paris/Tunis/Södertälje pickup, `_etaSeconds` is computed against that point, and the resumed `emit()` sets `_acceptedAt ??= now` / `_waitingSince ??= now` (lines 328-333) which `DriverTrackingController` adopts (`acceptedAt = event.acceptedAt ?? acceptedAt`) so the free-cancel/waiting clocks restart at reload time. Reproduced: a Paris trip resumed via `primeResume(driverArriving)`: `AUDIT D: resumed event lat=59.3365 lng=18.0638 eta=102s acceptedAt=<now>`.
failure_scenario: Demo build (R-web: 'a live ride must survive browser reload'). Rider books Gare du Nord -> Louvre (Q7 Paris zone) or a Södertälje pickup, gets a driver, reloads the tab: the driver marker appears in central Stockholm, the ETA reads ~2 min then jumps, the car 'arrives' and the trip starts from a point tens or hundreds of km from the pickup, and the free-cancel countdown restarts from the reload.
evidence:
mock_ride_realtime.dart:179-184 `if (resumeStatus != null && resumeStatus.isMatched) { ... _pickupLat ??= 59.3293; _pickupLng ??= 18.0686;`
mock_ride_realtime.dart:209-211 `lastLat ??= _pickupLat! + 0.0072; lastLng ??= _pickupLng! - 0.0048; _startGps();`
mock_ride_realtime.dart:263-266 and 303-305 `_pickupLat ??= 59.3293; ... lastLat ??= _pickupLat! + 0.0072; ... _emit(RideStatus.driverAssigned); _startGps(); unawaited(_hydratePickup());`
mock_ride_realtime.dart:328-333 `} else if (status.isMatched) { _acceptedAt ??= DateTime.now().toUtc(); } if (status == RideStatus.driverWaiting) { _waitingSince ??= DateTime.now().toUtc(); }`
suggested_fix: Let `primeResume` (and the first assignment) take the pickup coordinates and the snapshot's `acceptedAt`/`waitingArrivedAt`; hydrate the pickup before emitting `driverAssigned`, and do not stamp `_acceptedAt`/`_waitingSince` with the resume time.

title: History record time is overwritten with the Done-tap time; receipt date uses savedAt which lifecycle refreshes move
description: `markCompleted` archives the trip with `endedAt` defaulting to now (completion time) (377-382, on_demand_ride_history_store.dart 197 `final ended = endedAt ?? DateTime.now();`). When the rider taps Done, `closeCompletedRide` archives again with the same `reservationId` and no `endedAt` (453-457), so `archive` replaces the record (146-148) and its `scheduledPickupAt` becomes the time the rider left the summary, which can be much later. Separately, the receipt's 'Date and time' comes from `DriverRepository._completedAtLabel(ride.savedAt)` (driver_repository.dart 59), and `savedAt` is rewritten by `persistCompletedStatus` (395-400) on each payment/rating event and by `RideSnapshotStore.touchCurrent` on every background/pagehide (ride_snapshot_store.dart 452) because completed-surface statuses are not terminal; after a restore `LastCompletedRide.remember(snapshot)` (ride_restore_coordinator.dart 383) therefore shows the last backgrounding time, not the completion time.
failure_scenario: Trip completes at 14:00; the rider leaves the app on the summary, backgrounds it a few times and taps Done at 14:40. Ride History lists the trip at 14:40, and after a reload the receipt's 'Date and time' shows the last time the app was backgrounded.
evidence: active_ride_controller.dart:453-457 `if (snapshot != null && snapshot.status.isCompletedSurface) { await OnDemandRideHistoryStore.archive(snapshot, terminalStatus: snapshot.status); }` ; on_demand_ride_history_store.dart:197 `final ended = endedAt ?? DateTime.now();` ; driver_repository.dart:59 `completedAt: _completedAtLabel(ride.savedAt),`
suggested_fix: Record a completion timestamp in the snapshot when `markCompleted` runs and pass it as `endedAt` on every later archive and to the receipt.

title: Reload during re-dispatch after a driver drop restores Waiting with the dropped driver; Waiting never reacts to a searching status
description: `DriverTrackingController._persistLiveStatus` skips terminal statuses (211-212), and `ActiveRideController.resumeSearchingAfterDriverCancel` explicitly does not persist (327-334), so after a driver drop the stored snapshot still says `driverArriving`/`driverAssigned` with the old driver until the next accept. A reload in that window (`RideRestoreCoordinator.surfaceFor`, 285-291) restores `WaitingForDriver` with `driver: snapshot.driver`. With `ApiRideRealtime` the first poll carries `searching`; `reassigned` is only derived when `poll.lastStatus?.isMatched` (api_ride_realtime.dart 193-199), which is null on a fresh poll, so the event is a plain `findingDriver`. `_onLiveTick` has branches only for `cancelledByDriver`, terminal and completed statuses (410-423); a searching status falls through to the normal sheet rendering, so the screen keeps the 'Driver found' headline (`_headlineFor` → `eta?.headline(status: findingDriver)`), the dropped driver's card, plate and message/call buttons, and no reassignment notice. The rider only learns a new driver was assigned when the next accept arrives; a second reload would restore Finding because `_persistLiveStatus` then saves `findingDriver`.
failure_scenario: Release build: driver accepts, then drops the ride; the rider reloads the web app (or the process is restarted) before the next driver accepts. Waiting shows the old driver as 'on the way' while the server is searching; messages go to a driver who is no longer on the trip.
evidence: driver_tracking_controller.dart:211-212 `if (!persistRideSnapshot || status.isTerminal) return;` ; active_ride_controller.dart:329-333 comment 'Snapshot persistence is deliberately not on this critical path ... remains the correct recovery record' ; api_ride_realtime.dart:193-194 `final reassigned = status.isSearching && (poll.lastStatus?.isMatched ?? false);` ; waiting_for_driver.dart:417-433 only `isTerminal`/completed branches before rendering
suggested_fix: Persist the `findingDriver` status (without driver) when the research starts, and have Waiting treat an incoming `isSearching` status the same way as `cancelledByDriver` (back to Finding).

title: Driver drop while a child route is open pops that route instead of Waiting; Waiting is left dead and Finding never restarts the search
description: `_onLiveTick` handles `cancelledByDriver` immediately and deliberately bypasses the route-current gate (lines 405-415). `_researchAfterDriverCancel` disposes tracking, reconciles the session back to `findingDriver`, sets `_leaving = true`, then does `final navigator = Navigator.of(context); if (navigator.canPop()) { navigator.pop(true); return; }` (651-659). The app has a single navigator (app.dart:34, MoveraSheet.show uses rootNavigator: true), so `pop(true)` pops whatever route is on top: the driver profile (`_openProfile`, 976), Chat (waiting_sheet_bits 215), the arrived sheet, the cancel/reason sheets, the Safety Kit or the RoutePickerPage opened by `_changeRoute`. Waiting itself stays mounted with `_leaving = true`, `_mapParked = true` and a disposed `DriverTrackingController`; `FindingDrivers._openWaiting` (finding_drivers.dart 535-557) never receives `true`, so `_resumeFindingAfterDriverCancel` never runs and `FindingDriverController.active` stays null. Reproduced with a throwaway widget test (Waiting pushed over a parent, DriverProfilePage pushed above it, `MockRideRealtime.cancelByDriver()`): output was `profile still mounted: false`, `waiting still mounted: true`, `waiting route result: null`, `session status: RideStatus.findingDriver`.
failure_scenario: Rider is on Waiting and opens the driver's profile (or chat, or the cancel sheet, or 'Change route'); the driver drops the ride. The profile page closes by itself, the rider lands back on a grey, parked Waiting screen showing the old driver with no live updates and no way to cancel (`_confirmCancel` returns on `_leaving`), while the server trip is back in `searching` and the next driver's acceptance is never shown.
evidence: waiting_for_driver.dart:410-415 `if (status == RideStatus.cancelledByDriver) { if (!_leaving && !_completedOpened) { unawaited(_researchAfterDriverCancel()); } return; }` ; 651-659 `final navigator = Navigator.of(context); if (navigator.canPop()) { _researching = false; navigator.pop(true); return; }` ; movera_sheet.dart:48-51 `Navigator.of(context, rootNavigator: true).push<T>(route)` ; finding_drivers.dart:556 `if (!mounted || researchDriver != true) return;`
suggested_fix: Pop Waiting's own route by reference (store `ModalRoute.of(context)` in initState and use `Navigator.of(context).popUntil`/`removeRoute` on that route, or `closeRouteByReference`-style logic), or defer the research until `_routeIsCurrent` like the other stage navigations do.

title: `_confirmCancel` has no busy guard across its first await, so a double tap opens two stacked non-dismissible cancel sheets
description: `_confirmCancel` returns early only on `_leaving`, which is set at line 820, after two awaits: `await _cancelFeeNote()` (which itself awaits `RouteChangeController.storedRide()` -> SharedPreferences and `AppScope.instance.riderConfig.forZone(zone.id)`, lines 770-779) and `await showCancelRideSheet(...)`. The same handler is wired to the round cancel button (`MoveraIconButton.round(onPressed: _confirmCancel)` line 1498), to the in-trip panel's 'End trip here' (`onCancel: _confirmCancel` line 1890) and to the PopScope back handling (line 1450). `MoveraIconButton` is a plain `InkWell` with no debounce. Two taps during the fee lookup therefore run two `_confirmCancel` bodies; each calls `showCancelRideSheet`, which opens `MoveraSheet.show` with `swipeDismissible: false, barrierDismissible: false` (cancel_ride_sheet.dart:24-27) and only records `SheetCoordinator.instance.open(RideSheet.cancel)` (a plain field write, sheet_coordinator.dart:27). The second sheet is pushed on top of the first. If the rider taps 'Keep ride' on the top sheet, the first sheet is still there and must be dismissed again; if the rider confirms on the top sheet, the first body's continuation resumes only after the screen navigated away (`if (!mounted) return;`), and a second server cancel is avoided only because `PendingCancelStore.enqueue` reuses the existing entry's idempotency key.
failure_scenario: On the Waiting-for-driver screen the rider taps the X (cancel) button twice quickly while the fee note is being looked up. Two 'Cancel ride?' sheets stack; tapping 'Keep ride' closes only the top one and the rider sees the same sheet again and has to tap 'Keep ride' a second time (the sheet cannot be swiped or tapped away).
evidence: waiting_for_driver.dart:802-806 `Future<void> _confirmCancel() async { if (_leaving) return; final feeNote = await _cancelFeeNote(); if (!mounted || _leaving) return; final outcome = await showCancelRideSheet(` | :820 `_leaving = true;` | :1498 `onPressed: _confirmCancel,` | :1890 `onCancel: _confirmCancel,` | cancel_ride_sheet.dart:23-27 `SheetCoordinator.instance.open(RideSheet.cancel); final confirmed = await MoveraSheet.show<bool>( context: context, swipeDismissible: false, barrierDismissible: false,` | sheet_coordinator.dart:27 `void open(RideSheet sheet) => current = sheet;`
suggested_fix: Add a `_cancelSheetOpen`/`_cancelBusy` flag set synchronously at the top of `_confirmCancel` and cleared in a `finally`, or check `SheetCoordinator.instance.current == RideSheet.cancel` before opening; disable the cancel buttons while the flag is set.

title: Back gesture while the Waiting cancel/end-early request is in flight pops Waiting; Finding underneath stays parked and the cancel result is lost
description: `_confirmCancel` sets `_leaving = true; setState(() {});` (820-821) before `await _ride.markCancelled(...)` (838). `PopScope(canPop: _leaving, ...)` (1441) therefore lets a system back pop Waiting while the server request is still out (up to two attempts with 15 s timeouts each). The `_cancelling` overlay only blocks pointer input, not back. After the pop, `if (!mounted) return;` (846) discards the outcome: if the server confirmed, `_commitCancelled` already cleared the snapshot and set the session to `cancelledByRider` but `RideNavigator.home` is never called; if it was `pendingRetry`/`rejected`, the ride stays live with no screen. Waiting was pushed by `FindingDrivers._openWaiting` with `await Navigator.push<bool>` (finding_drivers.dart 535-556); the pop returns null, so `researchDriver != true` and Finding remains with `_leaving = true`, `_mapParked = true` and a disposed `_match` (528-531): a blank parked screen whose close button is inert (`_confirmCancel` returns on `_leaving`, 568).
failure_scenario: On Waiting the rider confirms 'Cancel ride', the network is slow, and they press the Android back button during the 'Cancelling…' card. Waiting disappears and the rider sees a dead grey Finding screen; depending on the server answer the ride is either cancelled with no Home navigation or still live with no way to see or cancel it from this screen.
evidence: waiting_for_driver.dart:819-821 `if (!outcome.cancelled) return; _leaving = true; setState(() {});` ; 837-846 `setState(() => _cancelling = true); final result = await _ride.markCancelled(...); if (!mounted) return;` ; 1441-1443 `PopScope(canPop: _leaving, onPopInvokedWithResult: (didPop, _) async { if (didPop) return;` ; finding_drivers.dart:556 `if (!mounted || researchDriver != true) return;`
suggested_fix: Keep `canPop` false while `_cancelling` is true (set `_leaving` only after the outcome is known), or handle `didPop` by finishing the flow from the result.

title: A pasted international number (+46 …) is rejected as an invalid Swedish mobile at sign-in
description: `AuthPhoneField` filters input to digits and spaces (auth_controls.dart:289-292), so a pasted `+46 70 123 45 67` becomes `46 70 123 45 67`. `swedishNumberFromField` then prefixes `+46` to anything not starting with `0` (993) giving `+4646701234567`; `toE164` sees 11 digits after +46 and returns null, so the screen shows "invalid Swedish mobile" for a valid number the rider pasted from Contacts.
failure_scenario: Rider pastes their number from the clipboard/contacts in international format on Sign in or Add phone; Continue is refused with an "invalid" error.
evidence:
auth_controls.dart:289-292 `inputFormatters: [FilteringTextInputFormatter.allow(RegExp(r'[0-9 ]')), LengthLimitingTextInputFormatter(14)],`
auth_navigation.dart:990-994 `final digits = typed.replaceAll(RegExp(r'\s+'), '').trim(); ... return SwedishPhone.toE164(digits.startsWith('0') ? digits : '+46$digits');`
suggested_fix: Strip a leading `46`/`0046` before prefixing, or pass the raw digits to `toE164` which already handles `46…`/`0046…` prefixes.

title: Sign-in hero tagline 'Moving to a new era.' is English although brandTagline is translated in the ARB
description: The sign-in hero (sign_in.dart:164 `hero: BalloonBrandIntro(progress: _story)`) draws `Text('Moving to a new era.', ...)` (:95) and a Semantics label 'Movera. Moving to a new era.' (:26). The ARB defines brandTagline with French/Swedish translations (' · Vers une nouvelle ère', ' · På väg mot en ny era') and rider_name.dart:140 uses it, so the same slogan appears translated on the next screen but English on Sign in when the zone default is fr/sv.
failure_scenario: App started in the France zone: Sign in shows 'Moving to a new era.' while Rider name shows 'Movera · Vers une nouvelle ère'.
evidence: balloon_brand_intro.dart:95 `'Moving to a new era.',`; :26 `label: 'Movera. Moving to a new era.',`; app_fr.arb:762 `"brandTagline": " · Vers une nouvelle ère"`
suggested_fix: Render the translated tagline (strip the leading ' · ' or add a dedicated key) in the intro and its Semantics label.

title: Finding's realtime listener treats a driver drop (cancelledByDriver) as a terminal end: archives the ride as cancelled, clears the snapshot and sends the rider Home while the server trip is back in searching
description: `RideStatus.cancelledByDriver` is in `isTerminal` only so the UI stops tracking the old driver; the trip itself is back in `searching` (core/contracts/ride_status.dart 31-36, trip_status.dart 134). Waiting handles it as a reversible re-dispatch, but the Finding listener does `if (event.status.isTerminal) { unawaited(_completeTerminal(event.status)); return; }` (394-397), and `_completeTerminal` archives `cancelledByDriver` to History as a cancelled ride (1027-1035), clears the snapshot and fires `_onTerminal`, which shows the 'Driver cancelled … Continue' sheet and `RideNavigator.home` (finding_drivers.dart 330-334). The event is reachable while Finding is still the subscriber: `ApiRideRealtime` maps a matched→searching projection to `cancelledByDriver` (api_ride_realtime.dart 193-199), and Finding stays subscribed after an accept whenever `_completeAssigned` is deferred (`_assignmentPending` because an offer raise/pickup edit or a cancel is in flight, 939-945) or during the `_persistAssigned` await before `_openWaiting` disposes the controller.
failure_scenario: Rider raises the offer; while the PATCH is out a driver accepts and immediately drops the ride. The next poll delivers `cancelledByDriver` to Finding: the ride is filed in History as cancelled, the snapshot is cleared and the rider is sent Home, although the server trip is still searching and may be accepted by another driver.
evidence: finding_driver_controller.dart:394-397 `if (event.status.isTerminal) { unawaited(_completeTerminal(event.status)); return; }` ; 1027-1035 archives when `status == RideStatus.cancelledByDriver` ; core/contracts/ride_status.dart:31-35 'the server put the trip back to `searching` ... Kept in [RideStatusX.isTerminal] only so the UI stops tracking the old driver; it is never a terminal status on the wire.'
suggested_fix: In the Finding listener treat `cancelledByDriver` as 'back to searching' (reset `_assigned`/`_assignmentPending`, keep the search) instead of routing it to `_completeTerminal`.

title: Unawaited `_store.save(...)` in the search-delayed path drops storage errors as unhandled async exceptions
description: `_evaluatePhase` fires `_store.save(_ordered(snapshot).copyWith(status: RideStatus.searchDelayed, ...))` without awaiting or catching. `RideSnapshotStore.save` (ride_snapshot_store.dart:355-404) awaits `PreferencesStore.load()` and `prefs.setString(key, encoded)` with no try/catch of its own, so a platform-channel/storage failure (quota, private-mode web storage, plugin error) becomes an unhandled asynchronous error raised from a periodic timer tick rather than being logged like the other `AppLog.warning` paths in this controller.
failure_scenario: On a device/browser where SharedPreferences writes fail (e.g. Safari private mode storage quota), the search passes the 'delayed' threshold; the timer tick's unawaited save throws and the error reaches the zone's unhandled-error handler (crash report / console noise) while the search itself continues.
evidence: finding_driver_controller.dart:586-594 `final snapshot = _snapshot; if (snapshot != null) { _store.save( _ordered(snapshot).copyWith( status: RideStatus.searchDelayed, savedAt: DateTime.now(), ), ); }` | ride_snapshot_store.dart:391-394 `final prefs = await PreferencesStore.load(); if (token != epoch) return; await prefs.setString(key, encoded);` (no try/catch)
suggested_fix: Wrap in `unawaited(_store.save(...).catchError((e) => AppLog.warning('ride.finding.snapshot_save_failed', ...)))` or await it inside the existing try path.

title: Cancel-first documentation says an unreachable server still commits the cancel locally; the code leaves the ride live (RC-03)
description: ARCHITECTURE.md lines 13-17 state that on Finding, Cancel request commits the ride as `cancelledByRider`, archives it and clears the snapshot 'on its OK — or when it cannot be reached, leaving the outbox entry to retry'. The method doc of `cancelSearch` repeats it (1089-1091: 'unreachable: the same local commit, with the outbox entry kept'). The implementation does the opposite: `if (result == SearchCancelResult.queued) { _cancelInFlight = false; _cancelQueued = true; ... return result; }` (1123-1137) commits nothing, keeps the search listening and shows 'Cancelling…'. The `SearchCancelResult.queued` enum comment (45-50) and the restore coordinator (111-117) describe this newer RC-03 behaviour, so the two records contradict each other and the architecture document no longer describes what the product does.
failure_scenario: An operator or tester reading ARCHITECTURE.md expects an offline cancel to land on Home with the ride archived; the app instead stays on the search screen with 'Cancelling…' until the server answers.
evidence: ARCHITECTURE.md:15-16 'on its OK — or when it cannot be reached, leaving the outbox entry to retry — the ride is committed as `cancelledByRider`, archived to History and `RideSnapshotStore.clear`ed' ; finding_driver_controller.dart:1090-1091 '- unreachable: the same local commit, with the outbox entry kept' ; 1123-1127 `if (result == SearchCancelResult.queued) { // RC-03: not committed. ...`
suggested_fix: Update ARCHITECTURE.md and the `cancelSearch` doc comment to the RC-03 behaviour (or restore the documented behaviour, whichever is the decision).

title: `_refreshRoadRoute` has no request generation, so an older road-route answer can overwrite the route drawn for a changed destination
description: `_adoptRoute` (line 395-406) and `_applyRouteChange` (line 700-711) update `_pickupPosition`/`_destinationPosition`, clear `_roadRoutePoints`, redraw, and then call `unawaited(_refreshRoadRoute())`. `_refreshRoadRoute` awaits `roadRoutePolyline(from: _pickupPosition, to: _destinationPosition)` (a network call via `RoutingService.roadLine`) and on return only checks `mounted` and `route.points.length < 2` before assigning `_roadRoutePoints = route.points` and redrawing. There is no check that the answer is for the route currently adopted. When a route change happens while the previous road request is still in flight (or a slow first request is beaten by the second), the older polyline lands last and is drawn between the new pickup/destination markers.
failure_scenario: Rider changes the destination from the Finding screen (or the server's route-change event arrives) right after the screen opened. The new destination marker appears, then the road line for the OLD destination is drawn on the map and stays until another route change or ride stage.
evidence: finding_drivers.dart:506-519 `Future<void> _refreshRoadRoute() async { if (_stops.isNotEmpty) return; final route = await roadRoutePolyline( id: 'route', from: _pickupPosition, to: _destinationPosition, color: RiderRouteStyle.color, ); if (!mounted || route.points.length < 2) return; _roadRoutePoints = route.points; _loadMapBits(); setState(() {}); }` | :403-405 `_roadRoutePoints = null; _loadMapBits(); if (_mapReady) unawaited(_refreshRoadRoute());` | :709-711 same in `_applyRouteChange`.
suggested_fix: Capture `from`/`to` (or a `++_routeGeneration`) before the await and discard the result when `_pickupPosition`/`_destinationPosition` changed (or the generation moved on) in the meantime.

title: History archives book-now rides with a UTC DateTime that is then rendered field-by-field, so times/dates show in UTC
description: recordFor stores `scheduledPickupAt: ended.toUtc()` (line 201) and `createdAt: snapshot.createdAt.toUtc()`. The History UI then formats that DateTime with helpers that read the DateTime's own fields rather than converting to local: ReservationFormat.time (lib/features/reservations/presentation/reservation_format.dart:70-74 uses `when.hour`/`when.minute`), ReservationFormat.moment/historyWhen (221-227 compare `when.year/month/day` to a local `DateTime.now()`), weekdayDate/_dayMonth via L10n.formatDate (intl formats the instance's fields; a UTC DateTime prints UTC), called from lib/features/history/presentation/ride_history.dart:546 `ReservationFormat.historyWhen(ride)`. HomeJourneySection.fromRides (lib/features/home/presentation/widgets/home_journey_section.dart:74-83) likewise buckets by `at.year/at.month` and `weeks[(at.day - 1) ~/ 7]` on the UTC value against a local `now`. The only consumer that converts, SupportController (`when: ride.scheduledPickupAt.toLocal()`), shows the correct intent. Verified by throwaway test: a ride ended at 14:30 CEST archived via recordFor and formatted with ReservationFormat.time gave '12:30'.
failure_scenario: Stockholm rider finishes a ride at 14:30 local (CEST). History lists it as '12:30'. A ride ended 00:40 on 1 May shows as 30 Apr 22:40 and is counted in April on the home 'Your month' card; near midnight the Today/Yesterday split is wrong. In Tunisia (UTC+1) every History time is one hour early.
suggested_fix: Either store `ended.toLocal()` in the archived Reservation (consistent with how book-later Reservations hold wall-clock local times) or make every formatter/aggregator call `.toLocal()` before reading fields (ReservationFormat.time/moment/cardDate/weekdayDate, HomeJourneySection.fromRides). Add a test with a UTC-constructed DateTime.

title: Server-backed History silently drops every fully settled trip (RideStatus.closed) and every paymentFailed trip
description: ApiRideHistoryRepository._record (lib/features/history/data/ride_history_repositories.dart:56-66) feeds each server TripProjection through RideProjection.toSnapshot and then OnDemandRideHistoryStore.recordFor(snapshot, terminalStatus: snapshot.status, ...). recordFor maps the status with _reservationStatus (lines 243-259), which returns ReservationStatus.completed only for status.isCompletedSurface (tripCompleted | paymentProcessing | paymentFinalized | ratingPending per lib/core/contracts/ride_status.dart:85-89) and ReservationStatus.cancelled only for an explicit cancelled list. RideStatus.closed (trip completed + payment settled + rating submitted/skipped) and RideStatus.paymentFailed are in neither branch, so _reservationStatus returns null and recordFor returns null (line 194), i.e. the trip is omitted from History. In release builds (ApiRideHistoryRepository) almost every finished trip the server returns is eventually `closed`, so the History tab loses the rider's past rides and their receipts; a payment-failed ride (which the rider must settle) also vanishes. Verified with a throwaway test (test/_audit_datamath_test.dart, since deleted): recordFor(...terminalStatus: RideStatus.closed) and paymentFailed both returned null while ratingPending returned a record (`3 passed` for these cases).
failure_scenario: Rider completes a trip, pays, rates the driver. Server projection now has status completed/paymentStatus settled/ratingStatus submitted -> RideStatusWire.fromTrip -> RideStatus.closed. The History screen loads /trips, _record returns null for it, and the ride (and every older settled ride) is not listed. A rider with 50 past trips sees an empty or near-empty History; a trip whose card payment failed also disappears, so the rider cannot see what is owed.
suggested_fix: In _reservationStatus treat RideStatus.closed and RideStatus.paymentFailed as ReservationStatus.completed (optionally carry a payment-failed flag on the Reservation for the receipt), or add a separate mapping for server trips in ApiRideHistoryRepository. Add a test that a `completed`+settled+rated projection appears in History.

title: History detail shows 'Movera Wallet' / 'Card' untranslated; only Cash is localized
description: The ride detail sheet prints `L10n.isCashLabel(ride.paymentMethod) ? context.l10n.payCash : ride.paymentMethod`. Rides booked with the wallet or the generic card row store the English names 'Movera Wallet' / 'Card' (`payment.name` in `_bookNow`), so in Swedish/French the line reads 'Betalsätt: Movera Wallet' while the Upcoming/Scheduled screens use `paymentLabelFor` (payment_labels.dart:24-29) and show 'Movera Plånbok' / 'Portefeuille Movera' for the same ride.
failure_scenario: Swedish UI, wallet-paid ride: History detail shows 'Betalsätt: Movera Wallet'; the reservation page for a scheduled wallet ride shows 'Movera Plånbok'.
evidence: ride_history.dart:551-555 `context.l10n.paymentMethodLine( L10n.isCashLabel(ride.paymentMethod) ? context.l10n.payCash : ride.paymentMethod, ),`; payment_labels.dart:24-29 `String paymentLabelFor(String stored) => switch (stored.trim()) { 'Cash' => L10n.current.payCash, 'Card' => L10n.current.payCard, 'Movera Wallet' => L10n.current.moveraWallet, _ => stored, };`; upcoming_reservation.dart:269 `paymentLabelFor(ride.paymentMethod),`
suggested_fix: Use `paymentLabelFor(ride.paymentMethod)` in the History detail sheet.

title: normaliseAddress forward-geocodes placeholder pickup labels, contrary to its own contract
description: isPlaceholderPickupLabel's doc says a placeholder 'must not be forward-geocoded or saved' (home_controller.dart:62-69), but normaliseAddress only short-circuits '' and 'Current location'. _showRouteAddressPicker normalises draft['pickup'] unconditionally (home.dart:954), and that value is locationOffPickupLabel when _prefillPickup fell back (home.dart:818-822) or pickupLocationFallbackLabel ('Pickup location') / a 'Dropped pin …' label when the pin was placed on the map (confirmedPickupAddress, pickup_address.dart:46-49). Reproduced with a recording geocoder: forward() was called with 'Location off, set pickup' and 'Pickup location'. With the in-process mock the text comes back unchanged (in_process_mock_client.dart returns `'address': normalized`), but any real geocoder that fuzzy-matches returns some place name, which then becomes the pickup label shown in SelectRide and sent with the booking while pickupLat/Lng stay at the pin or the Stockholm default.
failure_scenario: Staging build with a real geocoder. Rider chooses the pickup on the map; reverse geocode yields no street so the label is 'Pickup location'. After the picker pops, forward('Pickup location') returns e.g. a business called 'Pickup Location AB' in another city; SelectRide and the booking carry that label with the pin's coordinates.
evidence:
home_controller.dart:254-258 `Future<String> normaliseAddress(String input, {int? generation}) async { final clean = input.trim(); if (clean.isEmpty || clean == 'Current location') return clean; final scope = generation ?? _normaliseGuard.next(); final result = await geocoding.forward(clean);`
home_controller.dart:62-63 `/// Whether [label] is a placeholder rather than a real address, so it must /// not be forward-geocoded or saved.`
home.dart:954 `_normaliseAddress(rawPickup, generation: normaliseBatch),`
suggested_fix: Return early in normaliseAddress when isPlaceholderPickupLabel(clean) || needsDroppedPinLabel(clean), and skip normalising the pickup when the draft already carries pickupLat/Lng.

title: Home's load() keeps only 8 custom places and persist() writes that truncated list back, deleting the rest
description: HomePlacesController.load() maps `saved.places ... .take(maxCustom)` (8) into savedPlaces, and persist() writes `places: savedPlaces.map((place) => place.toJson()).toList()` to the shared HomeAddressRepository keys. SavedPlacesController.save() has no cap and appends freely (saved_places_controller.dart:98-99). Home persists on every booking/route change (_showRouteAddressPicker -> _persistAddressData, home.dart:1003) and after any saved-place edit, so the first Home persist after a 9th place exists removes places 9+ from storage for good. Reproduced: 9 stored places -> load gives 8 -> persist stores 8 (test output `loaded 8 of 9`, `stored after persist: 8`).
failure_scenario: Rider adds nine custom places in Menu > Saved places. They book a ride from Home; _persistAddressData runs and the ninth place disappears from Saved places permanently.
evidence:
home_places_controller.dart:67-70 `savedPlaces = saved.places.map(...).take(maxCustom).toList();`
home_places_controller.dart:73-81 `Future<void> persist() { return _store.save(HomeAddressSnapshot(... places: savedPlaces.map((place) => place.toJson()).toList())); }`
saved_places_controller.dart:98-99 `if (index < 0) { places.add(encoded); }` (no limit)
suggested_fix: Either enforce the same cap in SavedPlacesController.save, or keep the untruncated list (or re-read storage) when Home persists so it never writes fewer places than are stored.

title: Custom saved places are matched by type: editing or adding a second place of the same kind overwrites the first
description: Saved Places (SavedPlacesController.save, FLOW-5) deliberately allows several custom places of the same kind, each with its own id (saved_places_controller.dart:84-102). Home's edit path ignores ids: SavedPlacesRow long-press passes only `place.type` (saved_places_row.dart:108-110), _editSavedPlace -> _showAddressPicker(target:'custom', customType) -> _saveAddressFor -> applyResolved, which does `savedPlaces.indexWhere((place) => place.type == type)` and rewrites that first match. Home's Add place picker (home.dart:1359-1461) has the same effect: choosing a type that already exists replaces that place's address instead of adding one. Reproduced with a throwaway test: two gyms (ids a,b); applyResolved(custom, 'New street 9', 'gym') changed a to 'New street 9' and left b untouched (output: `after edit: [a:New street 9, b:Street B 2]`).
failure_scenario: Rider has 'Gym A' and 'Gym B' saved from Saved Places. On Home they long-press the Gym B card and enter a new address: Gym A's address is replaced, Gym B is unchanged, and the change is persisted. Likewise 'Add place > Gym' with an existing gym silently overwrites it.
evidence:
home_places_controller.dart:131-142 `case 'custom': final type = customType ?? 'other'; final existingIndex = savedPlaces.indexWhere((place) => place.type == type); if (existingIndex >= 0) { ... savedPlaces[existingIndex] = SavedPlaceData(id: existing.id, ... address: address); }`
saved_places_row.dart:108-110 `onLongPress: onEditSavedPlace == null ? null : () => onEditSavedPlace!('custom', customType: place.type),`
saved_places_controller.dart:50-51 `/// ... a second "Gym" is added next to the first instead of replacing it.`
suggested_fix: Pass the SavedPlaceData id (or index) through onEditSavedPlace/_showAddressPicker/applyResolved and match on id; for Add place with an existing type, append a new entry (as Saved Places does) or ask.

title: Custom place added from Home gets the raw type key as its title ('gym', 'restaurant', 'other') shown verbatim in every locale
description: applyResolved creates `SavedPlaceData(title: type, type: type, address: address)` and persist() stores 'title': 'gym'. _CustomPlaceCard renders `place.title` (saved_places_row.dart:239-240) and the Saved Places screen renders the stored title (saved_places_controller.dart:177-180 uses the title whenever non-empty), so the card reads 'restaurant' / 'other' in lowercase English even in the Swedish/French UI, while RoutePickerPage shows the localized placeLabelFor(place.type) for the same place. Reproduced: applyResolved(custom, customType:'restaurant') -> title 'restaurant'.
failure_scenario: Swedish rider taps Add > Restaurang on Home and saves an address; the Home card and Menu > Sparade platser list the place as 'restaurant'.
evidence:
home_places_controller.dart:143-146 `} else if (savedPlaces.length < maxCustom) { savedPlaces.add(SavedPlaceData(title: type, type: type, address: address)); }`
saved_places_row.dart:239-240 `TextWidget(text: place.title,`
suggested_fix: Store the localized label (placeLabelFor(type)) or leave title empty and let the UI derive it from type.

title: Location permission is requested again immediately after the rider denies it, and again on every app resume
description: _awaitCurrentFix loops two attempts; if the first detectCurrent returns quickly with permissionDenied (target == null), the second attempt starts a fresh detectCurrent, which calls location.requestPermission() again (home_controller.dart:369-371) — a second system prompt right after the first 'Deny'. didChangeAppLifecycleState(resumed) also calls _detectCurrentAddress() whenever _currentLatLng == null (home.dart:266-267), so an Android rider who denied once gets the prompt on each return to the app until Android auto-blocks it. iOS/web report deniedForever after one refusal, so only Android (and 'denied' on older Android indefinitely) is affected.
failure_scenario: Android rider taps Where to with location not yet granted, denies the prompt; within the same tap the prompt appears a second time (attempt 2). Later, every time they switch apps and come back, the prompt is shown again.
evidence:
home.dart:343-350 `for (var attempt = 0; attempt < 2; attempt++) { ... await _detectCurrentAddress().timeout(left, onTimeout: () {}); if (!mounted) return null; final fix = _tripPickupLatLng ?? _currentLatLng; if (fix != null) return fix; }`
