The same dot-only formatting reaches riders through toStringAsFixed with no locale: place_suggestion.dart:66-70 formatDistanceKm ('1.2 km'), ride_check_trigger.dart:244, trip_detail.dart:203 kmDriven, home_journey_section.dart:366 homeCo2Kg, ride_check_page.dart:44-50 and ride_check_demo_page.dart:159. Reproduced: L10n.use('sv'); formatMoney(Money(3550)) == '35.50 kr'.
failure_scenario: Swedish rider sees a cancellation fee of '35.50 kr', '4.2 km parcourus' / '4.2 km körda' on the receipt and '1.5 kg' CO2 on Home, where Swedish/French convention is '35,50 kr', '4,2 km', '1,5 kg'.
evidence: money.dart:31-33 `final major = money.majorString;\n      final isWhole = money.amountMinor % Money.minorPerMajor('SEK') == 0;\n      return '${isWhole ? major.split('.').first : major} kr';`; place_suggestion.dart:70 `: '${rounded.toStringAsFixed(1)} km';`; trip_detail.dart:203 `return L10n.current.kmDriven(km.toStringAsFixed(km < 10 ? 1 : 0));`
suggested_fix: Route fractional numbers through NumberFormat.decimalPattern(L10n.code) (or a small helper that swaps the separator for fr/sv) in money.dart and the distance/weight helpers.

title: HorizontalSwipe keeps drag state in build-local variables, so any rebuild mid-drag resets the origin and a leftward drag fires onSwipeRight (or is swallowed)
description: `start` and `last` are plain locals declared inside `build()` and captured by the three drag closures. GestureDetector re-syncs recognizer callbacks on every rebuild (RawGestureDetectorState.didUpdateWidget -> _syncAll re-initialises onStart/onUpdate/onEnd), so if the widget rebuilds while a finger is down, onUpdate/onEnd run with a fresh `start = 0`. `distance = last - start` then equals the absolute x position of the finger (always > 56 on a phone), so `right` is true regardless of direction. Callers: lib/features/home/presentation/home.dart:2177 wraps the Home sheet inside an AnimatedBuilder (rebuilds on every sheet tick and on every Home setState, e.g. each GPS fix delivered by HomeLocationController._deliverFix) with only onSwipeLeft -> a slow left swipe is swallowed and a fast one is cancelled because both `left` and `right` are true; lib/features/home/presentation/widgets/home_tab_page.dart:42 sets both callbacks, so a rebuild during a leftward drag pops the page with `HomeTabs.previousOf(tab)` (the wrong neighbour). Reproduced with a throwaway widget test (deleted): a 100 px leftward drag with one setState mid-drag printed `left=0 right=1`; the identical drag without the rebuild gave `left=1 right=0`.
failure_scenario: Rider on Home drags the sheet left to open Payment while a location fix arrives (Home rebuilds ~1 Hz): nothing opens, or on a bottom-bar page the app pops to the previous tab instead of the next one.
evidence: lib/shared/widgets/horizontal_swipe.dart:22-23 `double start = 0; double last = 0;` (inside build) ... :26 `onHorizontalDragStart: (d) => start = last = d.globalPosition.dx,` :30 `final distance = last - start;` :32 `final right = velocity > _minVelocity || distance > _minDistance;` ; lib/features/home/presentation/home.dart:2177 `child: HorizontalSwipe(` under `AnimatedBuilder` (~home.dart:2105); lib/features/home/presentation/widgets/home_tab_page.dart:42-45. Test run: `left=0 right=1 ... Expected: <1> Actual: <0>`.
suggested_fix: Make HorizontalSwipe a StatefulWidget (or keep start/last in a ValueNotifier/record owned outside build) so the drag origin survives rebuilds; alternatively use DragStartDetails/DragEndDetails only (d.velocity + accumulated delta from onHorizontalDragUpdate stored in State).

title: RouteTimeMarker caches one rendered PNG BitmapDescriptor per distinct label forever; labels change every minute so the cache grows for the app's lifetime
description: `_cache` is a static map keyed by `'$pickup|$label'` with no eviction. Callers render time-bearing labels: lib/features/ride_selection/presentation/select_ride.dart:869-872 `RouteTimeMarker.createIcon(pickup: false, label: context.l10n.arriveBy(_arrivalFor(ride)))` for every ride category (the arrival time advances each minute while Select Ride is open or re-opened), and lib/features/finding_driver/presentation/finding_drivers.dart:487-493 with ETA labels. Each entry holds a 3x-scale PNG (`imagePixelRatio: scale`, canvas ~ (bubbleW+24)x(bubbleH+~70) px) that is never released. Over a long session (several bookings, Select Ride left open) this is tens of MB of retained image bytes; the other marker caches are bounded by boolean/int keys, this one is not.
failure_scenario: Rider keeps the app open across a day of bookings: memory climbs by one PNG descriptor per (category x minute) label; on low-memory web/iOS PWA this contributes to tab eviction.
evidence: lib/shared/widgets/movera_map_markers.dart:235-236 `static final Map<String, Future<BitmapDescriptor>> _cache = <String, Future<BitmapDescriptor>>{};` :245 `return _cache.putIfAbsent('$pickup|$label', () async {` ... :317-320 `return BitmapDescriptor.bytes(data.buffer.asUint8List(), imagePixelRatio: scale);` (no removal anywhere); select_ride.dart:870-872 `RouteTimeMarker.createIcon(pickup: false, label: context.l10n.arriveBy(_arrivalFor(ride)),`
suggested_fix: Bound the cache (small LRU, e.g. keep the last ~16 labels) or key only on the current screen's labels and clear on dispose.

title: 'Open settings' in the push primer calls Geolocator.openAppSettings, which throws UnsupportedError on web
description: `_openSettings` defaults to `Geolocator.openAppSettings`. geolocator_web implements it as `throw _unsupported('openAppSettings')`. The primer is reachable on web in release-like builds (gate `enabled = !allowsMockTransport`): when the browser's `Notification.requestPermission()` answers 'denied' (or 'default'), `FlutterFirebasePushGateway.requestPermission` maps it to `PushAuthorizationStatus.denied`, `PushPermissionGate._register` stores `blockedBySystem`, and both the sheet (`_blocked`) and the Notifications screen banner then offer 'Open settings'. Tapping it throws inside the button callback; nothing opens, the rider gets no feedback, and the error is recorded as a crash by the zone handler. The location notice already handles this case correctly via `locationSettingsOpenerFor(isWeb: ...)` returning null, so the web branch was simply missed here.
failure_scenario: Staging web build, rider taps 'Turn on' and declines the browser notification prompt. Next visit to Notifications shows 'Ride updates are off' -> 'Open settings'; tapping does nothing visible and logs `zone.error UnsupportedError: openAppSettings() has not been implemented on the web`.
evidence: lib/shared/widgets/push_permission_primer.dart:85-86 `Future<void> _openSettings() async { await (widget.openAppSettings ?? Geolocator.openAppSettings)(); }`; line 149 `onPressed: _busy ? null : (_blocked ? _openSettings : _turnOn)`; geolocator_web-4.1.4/lib/geolocator_web.dart `Future<bool> openAppSettings() => throw _unsupported('openAppSettings');`; lib/core/notifications/push_permission_gate.dart:83-86 stores blockedBySystem on PushPermissionDeniedException.
suggested_fix: On web hide the settings action (or show copy explaining the browser's site-permission UI) the way `locationSettingsOpenerFor` does; wrap the call in try/catch and show a toast on failure.

title: screenHorizPadding is a lazily-initialised top-level double computed from ScreenUtil once, so it ignores later ScreenUtil re-initialisation (window resize) and can be read before ScreenUtilInit
description: `double screenHorizPadding = ScreenUtil().setWidth(16);` is evaluated on first read and never again. lib/app/screen_scale.dart:45-47 deliberately rebuilds ScreenUtilInit with new bounds on a window resize so widths rescale, but every consumer of this global (lib/features/messages/presentation/chat.dart:107-314, lib/features/home/presentation/home.dart:1990-2002, lib/features/ride_complete/presentation/trip_detail.dart:28, driver_info.dart:40) keeps the padding computed for the first window size while the rest of the layout (ResSize.w, which is a getter) rescales. If the first read happens before ScreenUtilInit has run (any host that builds one of those widgets directly) the value is derived from ScreenUtil's uninitialised defaults for the rest of the process.
failure_scenario: Desktop/web rider resizes the browser window from phone width to 1280 px: everything scaled through ResSize.w grows to the 1.25 bound, but the side gutters in Chat, Home's location card and Trip detail stay at the old 16 x (old scale) value, leaving misaligned edges.
evidence: lib/shared/widgets/responsive_size.dart:3 `double screenHorizPadding = ScreenUtil().setWidth(16);` ; lib/app/screen_scale.dart:45-47 `// The root View provides this MediaQuery, so a window resize rebuilds // ScreenUtil with new bounds.` ; home.dart:1990 `left: screenHorizPadding,`
suggested_fix: Make it a getter: `double get screenHorizPadding => ScreenUtil().setWidth(16);`.

title: CODE-14 'machine-specific generated files are not tracked' silently passes when git is unavailable
description: The test runs `git ls-files -ci --exclude-standard` and `return`s (passing) when the exit code is non-zero. That covers a tarball checkout, but it also covers a missing `git` binary, a sandboxed CI runner, or a `safe.directory` ownership refusal, in which case the guard is skipped without any signal.
failure_scenario: CI runner lacks git in PATH or refuses the directory as 'dubious ownership'; the test reports green while ignored-but-tracked files (the thing CODE-14 guards) go undetected.
suggested_fix: Only short-circuit when `Directory('.git').existsSync()` is false; otherwise fail with the git stderr so a broken runner is visible.

title: core -> features/di import guard only matches single-quoted package: imports; relative, double-quoted and conditional imports bypass it
description: The architecture guard extracts directives with `^\s*(?:import|export)\s+'([^']+)'` and then only flags URIs that start with `package:movera_rider/features/` or equal `package:movera_rider/app/di.dart`. A file under lib/core that writes `import '../../features/x/y.dart';`, `import "package:movera_rider/features/x/y.dart";`, or a `part`/deferred/conditional form reaches features without tripping the guard. Relative imports are already in use elsewhere in lib (e.g. lib/features/home/presentation/home_map_style.dart:1, lib/shared/widgets/custom_google_map.dart:12,14), so the style is not forbidden by lint. No current violation exists, so this is a gap in the gate, not a live breach.
failure_scenario: A developer adds `import '../../features/booking/application/booking_coordinator.dart';` to a file in lib/core; `flutter test test/architecture/guard_test.dart` still passes and the documented 'core is feature-agnostic' rule in ARCHITECTURE.md is silently broken.
evidence:
test/architecture/guard_test.dart:188-206:
```dart
    final directive = RegExp(
      r"^\s*(?:import|export)\s+'([^']+)'",
      multiLine: true,
    );
    ...
    for (final file in dartUnder('lib/core')) {
      for (final uri in importsOf(file.readAsStringSync())) {
        expect(
          uri.startsWith('package:movera_rider/features/') ||
              uri == 'package:movera_rider/app/di.dart',
          isFalse,
```
suggested_fix: Match both quote styles (`['"]([^'"]+)['"]`), resolve relative URIs against the file's directory before checking, and also reject any resolved path under lib/features or lib/app/di.dart; optionally add `always_use_package_imports` to analysis_options to make relative imports impossible.

title: Idempotency-key reuse/new-key tests are vacuous: failNext trips the quote call, so only one ride POST is ever observed and no keys are compared
description: Both 'failed finding retry reuses the same logical booking key' (lines 105-126) and 'changed finding intent receives a new booking key' (lines 128-161) set `RecordingMockClient()..failNext = true` and expect the first `submitFinding` to throw. But `BookingCoordinator.submitFinding` first calls `_resolveQuoteBinding` (POST /api/v1/quotes) before posting /api/v1/rides, and `InProcessMockClient.failNext` returns 500 to the next request of any path. So the 500 hits the quote request; the rides endpoint is never reached on the failed attempt, and `RecordingMockClient.send` (which only records POST /api/v1/rides, lines 19-26) records nothing. The second submit records exactly one key. Both tests then assert `hasLength(1)` and `isNotNull`, which is satisfied regardless of whether the coordinator reuses, rotates, or never sends an idempotency key. Neither test compares a key across attempts, so the 'reuse' and 'new key' semantics are untested. Reproduced with a throwaway test (test/_audit_lock_vacuous_test.dart, since deleted) recording request paths: after the failed submit, `rideKeys` was empty and exactly one `POST /api/v1/quotes` had been made; the second submit produced one ride key; `flutter test` output: `00:00 +1: All tests passed!`.
failure_scenario: A regression that generates a fresh Idempotency-Key on every retry (so a network blip double-books a ride), or that drops the header entirely on retry, passes both tests unchanged, while the test names claim the opposite is guaranteed.
suggested_fix: Make the failure hit the rides endpoint (e.g. a mock that fails only `POST /api/v1/rides` once, or pre-fetch the quote and pass the quote binding), then assert `idempotencyKeys` has length 2 and `keys[0] == keys[1]` for the retry case and `keys[0] != keys[1]` for the changed-intent case.

title: Empty `_guards()` body: the documented replacement guard for 'mock never invents a driver' asserts nothing
description: `_guards()` is called from main() (line 37) and carries a doc comment explaining it is 'The guard that replaces "the mock never invents a driver"' and that 'no screen, controller or feature repository may conjure a driver of its own'. Its body is empty, so the rule it documents is not enforced by any test in this file.
failure_scenario: A presentation widget or controller starts constructing a `MatchedDriver` locally when the API returns none; nothing in this test file fails, although its comment claims the invariant is guarded.
suggested_fix: Implement the guard (e.g. assert that no file outside lib/core/api constructs `MatchedDriver(` with literal mock identities, or that `MockDriverPool` is only referenced from the in-process mock client) or delete the empty function and its misleading comment.

title: 'duplicate assignment keeps last sequence' and 'stale out-of-order sequence' tests cannot fail on the behaviour they name
description: Line 33 asserts `seq.where((s) => s == 2).length >= 1` after emitting sequence 2 twice: it passes whether the duplicate is deduplicated, delivered twice, or reordered, so the dedup/last-sequence behaviour in the name is not verified. Lines 51-60 emit `driverAssigned` (seq 5) then `findingDriver` (seq 1) and assert only `contains(driverAssigned)`, which is trivially true because it was just emitted; whether the stale seq-1 event is dropped or applied (the actual ordering contract) is never asserted.
failure_scenario: MockRideRealtime (or a future replacement behind the same seam) starts delivering duplicate or stale-sequence events to subscribers; both tests still pass and downstream RideSession tests are the only line of defence.
suggested_fix: Assert the exact delivered list (e.g. `expect(seq, [2])` or `[2, 2]` depending on the intended contract, and `expect(statuses, [driverAssigned])` or `[driverAssigned, findingDriver]`) so the ordering/dedup contract is pinned.
